analyst_view.overall: Early view: Mainz are 12th and in a bad run under Urs Fischer, with one point from their first four home games and defeats to Bremen, Elversberg (4-1), Bochum in the cup and Bayern before the November break. Freiburg are third under Julian Schuster, have conceded only 10 league goals in 9 games and won four in a row in all competitions, but they host Panathinaikos in the Conference League on the Thursday before this Sunday afternoon game.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.0 goals. I lean lower: Freiburg are the tightest side in the top half (10 conceded in 9) and won 2-0 against Union while allowing four shots, and Fischer's Mainz are built on a deep 3-5-2 and transitions. Mainz have leaked goals lately, so the risk is a Freiburg win rather than an open game.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.2 corners. Nothing points clearly either way: Fischer's wing-backs and Freiburg's set pieces through Vincenzo Grifo both produce corners, but neither side plays a high-volume crossing game. I stay with the number for now.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.9 cards. I lean slightly higher: Mainz have had discipline problems this season, with Stefan Posch sent off at Elversberg and Phillipp Mwene banned after five yellows, and a home side short of points tends to chase duels. The referee is not known yet.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.3 shots. I lean lower: Freiburg are patient and give little away, and Schuster said himself they did not create many chances against Union. With Freiburg playing on the Thursday and likely to manage the game, I do not expect a shootout.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.9 shots on target. I lean a little lower for the same reasons as the shots: Freiburg's controlled style and a Mainz side that relies on Sheraldo Becker's runs in behind rather than volume. Team news in the final days could change this.
